pass_a_gloss: [...] For your sufferings I announce, and make widely shouted the misfortune brought upon you. And like some well-rhythmed lyre I will cry aloud, and I will strike thus, and make the song audible far, as the wall which you renewed. For the blessed prophet said at the beginnings of the vision: By night the Moabite land will perish; for by night the wall of the land of Moab will perish. And we, interpreting the force of the things said, were saying that, an earthquake having happened, the wall of the land of Moab broke down, and before the invasion of the enemies, all but levered up from foundations, it came thundering down over the [land] of the Moabites, which they also renewed, having spent wholly useless labour upon it. For Assyrians and Babylonians took the whole land without toil. My inward parts then will sound, he says, at your misfortunes like a harp, and so I will make your suffering widely shouted, just as indeed your wall was brought down, which you renewed, but for nothing of use. For the wall having fallen of itself, the thing that happened escaped none of those in all the [land] of the Moabites, or also of those being in other cities and countries. [Lemma, Isaiah 16:12:] And it will be, when you are put to shame, that Moab laboured at the altars, and she will enter into her handmade things so as to pray, and she will not be able to deliver him. And what besides this, he says, will happen again, which will come to you for shame and disgrace: for you will endure vain labours, filling up the altars beside you with bloods, and making the sacrifices unceasing, and bringing supplications to the handmade things. And you will obtain nothing of the things for benefit and safety. For they will not be able to free you from the evils hanging over you. For what strength is in lifeless idols, which are both findings of human art and have as craftsmen those who worship them? So, as the blessed David says: Let those who make them become like them, and all who have trusted in them. And it must be known that the Moabites were very much more superstitious, bird-watchers and false seers and wonder-tellers, and trusting very much in the evils from sorcery. For they thought perhaps to be able to prevail over the hand of the enemies, not so much, I think, by experience of tactics, as by the aids of the gods among them. But they missed their hope, calling lifeless matter to aid through sacrifices and supplication. [Lemma, Isaiah 16:13:] This is the word which the Lord spoke against Moab, when also he spoke. This, he says, is the vision spoken by God against the land of the Moabites; when also he spoke, that is, even if before the words through me came to be, he had spoken very many things about her, and on countless [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …For I proclaim your sufferings and make widely known the calamity brought upon you. Like a well-tuned lyre I will cry out; I will strike the strings so, and make the song heard far and wide, as with the wall which you renewed.

At the beginning of the vision the blessed prophet said: “By night the land of Moab will perish; for by night the wall of the land of Moab will perish” (Isaiah 15:1). In explaining the force of these words, we said that when an earthquake struck, the wall of the land of Moab burst apart, and before the enemy's invasion it was all but levered up from its foundations and came crashing down over the land of the Moabites. They renewed it, but spent their labour on it entirely in vain, for the Assyrians and Babylonians took the whole land without effort.

“My inward parts,” he says, “will sound like a harp” over your misfortunes (Isaiah 16:11), and so I will make your suffering known far and wide, just as your wall came down, the wall you renewed, but to no good purpose. For when the wall fell of itself, what had happened escaped no one in the whole land of the Moabites, nor those living in other cities and countries.
“And it will be, when you are put to shame, that Moab has wearied herself at the altars; and she will go into her handmade things to pray, and she will not be able to deliver him” (Isaiah 16:12).

Something more, he says, will happen to you besides, which will bring you shame and disgrace: you will endure labours in vain, filling your altars with blood, making your sacrifices unceasing, and offering prayers to things made by hands. You will obtain nothing that brings help or safety, for they will not be able to free you from the evils hanging over you.

What strength is there in lifeless idols, which are inventions of human skill and have for their makers the very people who worship them? So, as the blessed David says: “Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them” (Psalm 115:8).

It should be known that the Moabites were extremely superstitious: readers of bird omens, false prophets, and tellers of wonders, who put very great confidence in the evils of sorcery. For they perhaps supposed that they could prevail over the enemy's power, not so much, I think, by skill in tactics as by the help of their own gods. But they were disappointed in their hope, since they called lifeless matter to their aid with sacrifices and prayer.

“This is the word which the Lord spoke against Moab, when he spoke” (Isaiah 16:13). This, he says, is the vision spoken by God against the land of the Moabites; “when he spoke,” that is, even before the words came through me, he had spoken a great many things about her, and on countless…

choices.why: οὐδένα … ἔλαθεν τὸ συμβεβηκός: the fall of the wall escaped no one's notice; it is not that nothing was hidden.
rejected: none of the things that happened were hidden

choices.english: Moab has wearied herself at the altars
choices.why: Moab, not the idols, is the subject who labours at the altars.
rejected: the idols will labour in vain on the altars

choices.english: have for their makers the very people who worship them
choices.why: δημιουργοὺς ἔχουσι τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας: the worshippers are the craftsmen.
Describes the kind of diviner; plain English for the Greek term.
Set against trust in their gods; military skill is meant.
